metadata.title: Algebraic proof of Brooks' theorem
metadata.authors: Jan Hladky, Daniel Kral', Uwe Schauz

nodes.name: Even Eulerian subgraph
nodes.statement: An $\emph{even Eulerian subgraph}$ of an oriented graph $G$ is a spanning subgraph with an even number of edges such that every vertex has the same in-degree and out-degree.
nodes.statement_clean: Spanning subgraph with even edge count where each vertex has equal in/out-degree.

nodes.name: Odd Eulerian subgraph
nodes.statement: An $\emph{odd Eulerian subgraph}$ of an oriented graph $G$ is a spanning subgraph with an odd number of edges such that every vertex has the same in-degree and out-degree.
nodes.statement_clean: Spanning subgraph with odd edge count where each vertex has equal in/out-degree.

nodes.name: $(k+1)$-paintability (Paint and Correct game)
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ is $(k+1)$-paintable if Mrs.~Correct has a winning strategy in the marking game where each vertex starts with $k$ erasers; Mr.~Paint marks non-empty vertex subsets and Mrs.~Correct removes an independent subset of marked vertices and erases marks on the rest.
nodes.statement_clean: Graph property defined via the Paint-Correct game with $k$ erasers per vertex.

nodes.name: Gallai tree
nodes.statement: A $\emph{Gallai tree}$ is a graph in which every block is a complete graph or an odd cycle.
nodes.statement_clean: Graph whose blocks are all complete graphs or odd cycles.

nodes.name: List degree colorable
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ is $\emph{list degree colorable}$ if it can be colored from any list assignment $L$ where $|L(v)|$ equals the degree of $v$ for every vertex $v$.
nodes.statement_clean: Colorable from every list assignment matching vertex degrees.

nodes.name: Degree paintable
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ is $\emph{degree paintable}$ if Mrs.~Correct always wins the Paint-Correct game when each vertex $v$ starts with $\deg(v)-1$ erasers.
nodes.statement_clean: Mrs. Correct wins paintability game with $\deg(v)-1$ erasers per vertex.

nodes.name: Alon-Tarsi Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be an oriented graph and $d^+_v$ the in-degree of vertex $v$. If the numbers of even and odd Eulerian subgraphs of $G$ differ, then $G$ can be colored from any lists $L(v)$ with $|L(v)|\ge d^+_v+1$; in particular, if the maximum in-degree is $k$, $G$ is list $(k+1)$-colorable.
nodes.statement_clean: Differing parity counts of Eulerian subgraphs imply list colorability with lists of size $d^+_v+1$.
assumptions: the numbers of even and odd Eulerian subgraphs of $G$ differ
conclusions: $G$ can be colored from any lists $L(v)$ with $|L(v)|\ge d^+_v+1$
if maximum in-degree is $k$, $G$ is list $(k+1)$-colorable

nodes.name: Paintability via Eulerian subgraph parity
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be an oriented graph and $d^+_v$ the in-degree of vertex $v$. If the numbers of even and odd Eulerian subgraphs of $G$ differ, then Mrs.~Correct always wins the Paint-Correct game when each vertex $v$ has $d^+_v$ erasers; in particular, if maximum in-degree is $k$, $G$ is $(k+1)$-paintable.
nodes.statement_clean: Differing Eulerian parity counts imply paintability with $d^+_v$ erasers.
assumptions: the numbers of even and odd Eulerian subgraphs of $G$ differ
conclusions: Mrs.~Correct always wins when each vertex $v$ has $d^+_v$ erasers
nodes.origin_citation: Schauz, Flexible color lists in Alon and Tarsi's theorem (bib-uwe)

nodes.name: Brooks' Theorem
nodes.statement: Every connected graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta$ is $\Delta$-colorable unless $G$ is an odd cycle or a complete graph.
nodes.statement_clean: Connected graphs are $\Delta$-colorable unless they are odd cycles or complete graphs.
assumptions: $G$ is neither an odd cycle nor a complete graph

nodes.name: Structural lemma: even cycle with at most one chord
nodes.statement: Every connected graph $G$ that is not a Gallai tree contains an even cycle $C$ with at most one chord as an induced subgraph.
nodes.statement_clean: Non-Gallai-tree connected graphs contain an induced even cycle with at most one chord.
conclusions: $G$ contains an even cycle $C$ with at most one chord as an induced subgraph

nodes.name: DFS-style vertex ordering lemma
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph and $v$ an arbitrary vertex of $G$. The vertices of $G$ can be ordered so that every vertex except $v$ is preceded by at least one of its neighbors.
nodes.statement_clean: Connected graphs admit an ordering where each non-root vertex follows a neighbor.
conclusions: the vertices of $G$ admit an ordering in which every vertex other than $v$ is preceded by at least one of its neighbors

nodes.name: Algebraic Brooks' theorem (list degree colorability and degree paintability)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph. If $G$ is not a Gallai tree, then $G$ is list degree colorable and degree paintable.
nodes.statement_clean: Non-Gallai-tree connected graphs are list degree colorable and degree paintable.

nodes.name: Brooks' theorem (list and paintable version)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. If $G$ is neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle, then $G$ is list $\Delta$-colorable and $\Delta$-paintable.
nodes.statement_clean: Connected graphs that are not complete or odd cycles are list $\Delta$-colorable and $\Delta$-paintable.
assumptions: $G$ is a connected graph with maximum degree $\Delta$
$G$ is neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle

nodes.name: Claim 1: $G$ contains a non-complete non-odd-cycle inducing cycle
nodes.statement: The graph $G$ contains a cycle $C$ that induces neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle.
conclusions: $G$ contains a cycle $C$ inducing neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle

nodes.name: Claim 2: no universal vertex on shortest such cycle of length $\ge 5$
nodes.statement: Let $C=v_1\ldots v_{\ell}$ be the shortest cycle with the properties of Claim~1. If $\ell\ge 5$, then no vertex of $C$ is adjacent to all other vertices on $C$.
assumptions: $C=v_1\ldots v_{\ell}$ is the shortest cycle inducing neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle
conclusions: no vertex of $C$ is adjacent to all other vertices on $C$

nodes.name: Claim 3: each vertex of shortest such cycle has at most one chord
nodes.statement: Let $C=v_1\ldots v_{\ell}$ be the shortest cycle with the properties of Claim~1. Each vertex of $C$ is incident with at most one chord.
assumptions: $C=v_1\ldots v_{\ell}$ is the shortest cycle inducing neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle
conclusions: each vertex of $C$ is incident with at most one chord

nodes.name: Claim 4: shortest such cycle is even
nodes.statement: The shortest cycle $C=v_1\ldots v_{\ell}$ with the properties of Claim~1 is even.
assumptions: $C=v_1\ldots v_{\ell}$ is the shortest cycle inducing neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle

nodes.name: Claim 5: shortest such cycle has at most one chord
nodes.statement: The shortest cycle $C=v_1\ldots v_{\ell}$ with the properties of Claim~1 contains at most one chord.
assumptions: $C=v_1\ldots v_{\ell}$ is the shortest cycle inducing neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle

nodes.name: Proof of structural lemma
nodes.statement: Proof in five claims: choose a non-complete non-odd-cycle block, build the shortest cycle with the desired property, then bound the chords and parity via Claims~1--5.

nodes.name: Proof of DFS ordering lemma
nodes.statement: Take a spanning tree $T$ of $G$ rooted at $v$ and order vertices by levels of $T$; each non-root vertex is preceded by its parent.

nodes.name: Proof of algebraic Brooks' theorem
nodes.statement: Construct an orientation in which every vertex has out-degree $\ge 1$ and even/odd Eulerian-subgraph counts differ; conclude via Theorems~\ref{thm-alon-tarsi} and~\ref{thm-paint}.

nodes.name: Reduction to orientation existence
nodes.statement: It suffices to construct an orientation of $G$ such that each vertex has at least one out-going edge and the numbers of even and odd Eulerian subgraphs differ; Theorems~\ref{thm-alon-tarsi} and~\ref{thm-paint} then imply the claim.

nodes.name: Apply structural lemma to obtain even cycle $C$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lm-struct}, $G$ contains an even cycle $C$ with at most one chord.

nodes.name: Construct vertex ordering by contracting $C$
nodes.statement: Contract $C$ to a single vertex $w$, apply Lemma~\ref{lm-dfs} to the resulting graph, and produce an ordering $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ of $V(G)$ by re-expanding $w$ as $C$'s vertices in arbitrary order.

nodes.name: Define orientation: $C$ cyclic, others backward in order
nodes.statement: Orient edges of $C$ cyclically; for every edge $v_iv_j$ with $i<j$ not on $C$ (including the chord, if any), orient it from $v_j$ to $v_i$.

nodes.name: Enumerate Eulerian subgraphs and compare parities
nodes.statement: The orientation has exactly two even Eulerian subgraphs (the empty one and $C$); a chord $e$ adds at most one more Eulerian subgraph that is either even or odd, so the even/odd counts differ.

nodes.name: Conclude via Alon-Tarsi and paintability theorems
nodes.statement: Each vertex has at least one out-going edge by construction; combining with differing Eulerian parities, Theorems~\ref{thm-alon-tarsi} and~\ref{thm-paint} yield list degree colorability and degree paintability.

nodes.name: Claim 1: produce non-complete non-odd-cycle inducing cycle
nodes.statement: Pick a block $H$ of $G$ that is neither complete nor an odd cycle; the longest cycle $C_0$ of $H$ either gives the desired cycle or, by extending $C_0$ via a vertex $v$ off $C_0$ and a shortest path $P$ in $H\setminus v$, yields an even cycle $C_1$ that is not a complete subgraph.

nodes.name: Claim 2: forbid universal vertex on shortest cycle of length $\ge 5$
nodes.statement: If $v_1$ were adjacent to $v_2,\ldots,v_{\ell}$ on the shortest cycle $C$ with $\ell\ge 5$, the cycles $v_1\ldots v_{\ell-1}$ and $v_1v_3\ldots v_{\ell}$ would both induce complete graphs, but the cycle $v_1v_2v_3v_{\ell}$ would be a shorter witness, contradicting minimality.

nodes.name: Claim 3: at most one chord per vertex of shortest cycle
nodes.statement: For $\ell=4$ the conclusion is immediate; for $\ell\ge 5$, two chords $v_1v_a, v_1v_b$ with $3\le a<b\le \ell-2$ would give a shorter cycle with the Claim~1 property (using Claim~2), contradiction.

nodes.name: Claim 4: shortest such cycle is even
nodes.statement: If $C$ were odd it must have a chord $v_1v_i$; then one of $v_1\ldots v_i$, $v_1v_i\ldots v_{\ell}$ is even, must induce a complete graph, forcing $v_1$ adjacent to $v_3$ and $v_i$, contradicting Claim~3.

nodes.name: Claim 5: at most one chord total on shortest cycle
nodes.statement: Two chords $v_av_b$ and $v_cv_d$ either don't cross (giving a shorter Claim~1 cycle) or cross with all four arc-counts $n_{xy}$ same parity, in which case the shorter even cycle $v_a\ldots v_cv_d\ldots v_b$ would induce a complete graph violating Claim~3.

nodes.name: Combine Claims 4 and 5 to conclude lemma
nodes.statement: Claims~\ref{cl-3+} and~\ref{cl-4} together yield that the shortest such cycle is even with at most one chord, proving the structural lemma.

nodes.name: Choose spanning tree rooted at $v$
nodes.statement: Take an arbitrary spanning tree $T$ of $G$ and root it at $v$.

nodes.name: Order vertices by BFS levels
nodes.statement: List vertices level by level: root $v$ first, then all level-2 vertices, then level-3, etc.; each non-root vertex is preceded by its parent in $T$, which is a neighbor in $G$.

nodes.name: Paintability implies list colorability
nodes.statement: Every $(k+1)$-paintable graph is also list $(k+1)$-colorable; hence the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm-paint} given by Schauz also yields a combinatorial proof of Theorem~\ref{thm-alon-tarsi}.

nodes.name: Motivation: circular list colorings
nodes.statement: A Brooks-type theorem for circular list colorings remains open; an algebraic proof of classical Brooks is a natural first step toward addressing it.
